healthcareSystem: Well-developed for a Caribbean island. Curaçao Medical Center (CMC) is a modern facility. Private clinics available. Healthcare funded through social insurance system. Dutch standards influence quality.
qualityNotes: Decent healthcare by Caribbean standards. Curaçao Medical Center opened in 2019 and is a modern hospital. Dutch/Papiamentu are primary languages but English is widely understood. Specialist care may require transfer to the Netherlands, Colombia, or the US.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies (botica) open 8am-6pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturday. Duty pharmacies (botica di warda) operate after hours and weekends on rotation.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are well-stocked and professionally run. Dutch pharmaceutical standards apply. Papiamentu, Dutch, Spanish, and English spoken. Look for 'Botica' signs.
prescriptionRules: Dutch-style prescription system. Antibiotics and controlled substances require a prescription. Many basic medications available OTC. Local prescriptions may be needed for some medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging. Dutch rules apply.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis products
restrictedMeds.note: Unlike the Netherlands, cannabis is illegal in Curaçao.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all prescription medications. Keep medications in original packaging. English, Dutch, or Spanish documentation accepted.

travelInsurance.tips: Recommended for all visitors. Curaçao Medical Center provides good care but costs can be high. Ensure coverage includes diving, snorkeling, and water sports.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. No malaria. Dengue and Zika have been reported — use insect repellent.

waterNotes: Tap water in Curaçao is safe to drink. It is desalinated seawater and meets international standards. One of the few Caribbean islands with reliably safe tap water.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are good. Restaurants follow Dutch-influenced hygiene standards. Fresh seafood is excellent. Local dishes like keshi yena and stoba are safe at restaurants. Street food (such as from Plasa Bieu market) is generally safe.
medicalTourismNote: Curaçao is not a major medical tourism destination, though it receives some patients from nearby Venezuelan and other Caribbean islands due to its relatively modern hospital.
metaDescription: Health guide for Curaçao: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, safe tap water, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Curaçao Medical Center (CMC)
hospitals.notes: Modern hospital opened in 2019. Emergency department. Best medical facility on the island. Multilingual staff (Dutch, Papiamentu, English, Spanish).

hospitals.name: St. Elisabeth Hospital Outpatient Clinic
hospitals.notes: Outpatient services. Good for non-emergency care.

hospitals.name: Taams Medical Center
hospitals.notes: Private medical clinic. Walk-in appointments. Popular with tourists. Multilingual staff.

hospitals.name: Advent Hospital
hospitals.notes: Small private hospital. General and specialist care. English-speaking staff.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care available in Willemstad. Several private dental clinics.
dentalCare.notes: Dental clinics follow Dutch standards. Multilingual staff. Good quality care.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: CMC has emergency dental referrals. Several private dental practices in Willemstad accept walk-ins.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Willemstad. Many therapists speak Dutch, Papiamentu, English, and Spanish.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services available through CMC and private practitioners. Better resources than most Caribbean islands.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Moderate accessibility. Willemstad's Punda and Otrobanda historic districts have cobblestone streets. Modern hotels and CMC have good accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Curaçao Medical Center is modern and fully wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Limited accessible public transport. Taxis available. Many hotels offer shuttle services.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Modern resorts and hotels generally have good accessibility. Historic Willemstad can be challenging with cobblestones. Beach access varies — Mambo Beach has some accessible features. Confirm accessibility with specific hotels.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Available at CMC and private labs.
covidStatus.notes: Sun exposure, diving-related injuries, and dengue are more relevant health concerns for tourists.

insuranceClaimProcess: CMC accepts most international insurance. Upfront payment may be required (credit cards accepted). Keep all receipts. Documentation available in Dutch and English.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Local currency is Netherlands Antillean Guilder (ANG), pegged to USD. USD widely accepted.

medicalEvacuation.note: CMC handles most cases well. For highly specialized care, evacuation to Colombia (close and affordable) or the Netherlands (for Dutch citizens) is arranged.

drugNameMap.note: Dutch brands common. Paracetamol is the standard name.
